examples.en: The spot where I fell swelled up in just one area.

examples.ko: 문제가 국부적인 것이라서 금방 고칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: The problem is a localized one, so we can fix it quickly.

examples.ko: 이 약은 국부적 통증에 바르면 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine works when you apply it to localized pain.
The damage appeared only in certain spots, but I'm still very worried.

examples.ko: 국부적인 마취만 해서 수술 중에도 깨어 있었어요.
examples.en: I only had a local anesthetic, so I was awake during the surgery.

examples.ko: 이 병은 국부적 증상만 있어서 걱정하지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: This illness only has localized symptoms, so you don't need to worry.

explain: '국지적'과 비슷하지만 '국부적'은 몸이나 물건의 한 부분처럼 전체 중 일부를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 날씨나 지역 이야기에는 '국지적'을 더 자주 써요. 보통 '국부적으로', '국부적인'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '국지적', but '국부적' fits best when you talk about one part of a whole, like a body part or an object. For weather or regions, '국지적' is used more often. It usually appears as '국부적으로' or '국부적인'.

examples.en: The company succeeded in producing the key parts domestically.

examples.ko: 반도체 장비 국산화가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Domestic production of semiconductor equipment is moving fast.

examples.ko: 국산화 비율을 높이려고 연구를 많이 해요.
examples.en: They do a lot of research to raise the rate of domestic production.
The government announced it will support domestic production of parts.
After production moved domestic, repairs became much easier.

examples.ko: 이 제품의 국산화는 거의 끝났다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that the move to domestic production of this product is almost done.

explain: 주로 기계, 부품, 기술처럼 수입하던 것을 우리나라에서 만들게 될 때 써요. 뉴스와 경제 이야기에서 '부품 국산화', '국산화 비율'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대로 외국에서 들여오는 것은 '수입'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when something that used to be imported, such as machines, parts or technology, comes to be made in Korea. You often see it in news and economy talk, as in '부품 국산화' or '국산화 비율'. The opposite idea is '수입' (import).

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 이 기계를 국산화하려고 해요.
examples.en: Our company is trying to produce this machine domestically.
We cut costs by making the imported parts domestically.

examples.ko: 기술을 국산화하는 데 오 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five years to localize the technology.
We plan to produce all of this product domestically.
We started by producing the core equipment domestically.
Making the parts domestically is harder than I thought.

explain: '국산화'에 '하다'가 붙은 말로, 수입하던 물건이나 기술을 우리나라에서 만든다는 쓰임이에요. '~을/를 국산화하다' 형태로 쓰고, 회사나 정부 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '우리나라에서 만들다'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 국산화하다' for making goods or technology in Korea that used to be imported. It shows up mostly in talk about companies and government. In everyday speech, people may just say '우리나라에서 만들다'.

examples.ko: 국수주의를 따르는 사람들은 외국 문화를 싫어해요.
examples.en: People who follow ultranationalism dislike foreign cultures.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 국수주의적인 발언으로 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: That politician was criticized for his ultranationalist remarks.

examples.ko: 지나친 국수주의는 오히려 나라에 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Excessive ultranationalism actually doesn't help the country.
We learned about ultranationalism in history class.

examples.ko: 요즘 유럽에서 국수주의가 다시 늘고 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say ultranationalism is rising again in Europe these days.

examples.ko: 자기 나라만 최고라는 국수주의 생각은 위험해요.
examples.en: The ultranationalist idea that only your own country is the best is dangerous.

explain: 자기 나라의 것만 훌륭하다고 보고 다른 나라를 낮춰 보는 생각에 써서, 보통 좋지 않은 느낌이에요. 자기 나라를 아끼는 마음을 말하는 '애국심'과는 달라요. 번역할 때 'nationalism'보다 'ultranationalism'에 가까울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It carries a negative tone, for the view that only your own country's things are great and others are lesser. It is different from '애국심' (patriotism), which is just love for your country. In English it is often closer to 'ultranationalism' than plain 'nationalism'.

examples.en: His major is Korean linguistics.
I'm studying Korean linguistics at university.
In Korean linguistics, people study the sounds and grammar of the language.
My younger sibling is more interested in literature than in Korean linguistics.
Korean linguistics is hard too, but it's fun.
I got a book recommendation from a senior who majors in Korean linguistics.

explain: 한국 사람들이 '국어'라고 부르는 한국어를 연구하는 학문이에요. 말소리, 단어, 문법, 말의 역사를 다뤄요. 비슷한 말인 '국문학'은 글과 작품을 다루는 쪽이라 달라요.
explain_en: It is the field that studies Korean, which Koreans call '국어'. It covers sounds, words, grammar and the history of the language. It differs from '국문학', which deals with Korean literature and texts.

examples.en: This park was originally state-owned land.
You can't sell state-owned land as you please.

examples.ko: 산 대부분이 국유지라서 개인이 집을 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Most of the mountain is state-owned, so individuals can't build houses.

examples.ko: 국유지에 허락 없이 밭을 만들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not make a field on state land without permission.

examples.ko: 정부가 국유지 일부를 시민에게 빌려주기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to lend part of its land to citizens.

examples.ko: 이 땅이 국유지인지 사유지인지 확인해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's check whether this land is state-owned or private.

explain: 나라가 가진 땅을 말하고, 개인이 가진 '사유지'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 땅을 빌리거나 집을 지을 때, 또 뉴스에서 이 말을 들을 수 있어요. 시나 도가 가진 땅은 '공유지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means land owned by the state, and it often pairs with '사유지' (private land). You may hear it when renting land, building a house, or in the news. Land owned by a city or province is also called '공유지' (public land).

examples.ko: 그 나라는 석유 회사의 국유화를 발표했어요.
examples.en: That country announced the nationalization of its oil company.
Many people also oppose the nationalization of banks.
We debated whether nationalization would help the economy.

examples.ko: 철도 국유화는 역사 시간에 자주 나오는 주제예요.
examples.en: Railway nationalization is a topic that often comes up in history class.

examples.ko: 국유화 이후에 회사 직원들이 크게 걱정했어요.
examples.en: After the nationalization, the company's employees were very worried.
When the factory was nationalized, the boss changed too.

explain: 회사, 땅, 산업을 나라의 소유로 바꾸는 일이라서 경제와 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 반대로 나라의 것을 민간에 넘기는 일은 '민영화'라고 해요. '국영화'는 나라가 직접 운영한다는 점에 초점이 있어서, 소유를 말하는 '국유화'와 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It means turning a company, land or industry into state property, and it is common in economy and history talk. The opposite, handing state things over to private hands, is '민영화' (privatization). '국영화' focuses on the state running something, so it differs a little from '국유화', which is about ownership.

examples.en: The government is trying to nationalize that company.
The state nationalized the mines.

examples.ko: 모든 땅을 국유화하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Nationalizing all the land is not easy.
They say they got past the crisis by nationalizing the banks.

examples.ko: 국유화할 이유가 있는지 먼저 따져 봐요.
examples.en: Let's first consider whether there is a reason to nationalize it.
An opinion came up to nationalize the railways.

explain: '~을/를 국유화하다' 형태로 쓰고, 주어는 보통 정부나 나라예요. 기업이나 산업을 나라가 가져가는 일을 말해서 뉴스와 수업에서 주로 들을 수 있어요. 반대말처럼 쓰는 말은 '민영화하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 국유화하다', and the subject is usually the government or state. You mostly hear it in news and classes when the state takes over a company or industry. The opposite idea is '민영화하다' (to privatize).

examples.ko: 내일은 국지적으로 천둥이 칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: Tomorrow there may be thunder in some areas.

examples.ko: 이번 가뭄은 국지적인 현상이라서 다른 곳은 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This drought is a regional phenomenon, so other places are fine.
The road was blocked because of localized heavy rain.
The damage showed up in limited areas, so recovery was quick.

examples.ko: 국지적인 문제를 전체 문제처럼 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't talk about a local problem as if it were the whole problem.

examples.ko: 국지적 갈등이 점점 커지지 않을까 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that the local conflict might keep growing.

explain: 일기예보에서 '국지적으로 비가 오다'처럼 일부 지역에만 생기는 일에 많이 써요. '국부적'은 한 부분을 말할 때 더 어울리고, '국지적'은 지역을 말할 때 더 어울려요. 반대말은 '전국적'이에요.
explain_en: It is common in weather forecasts, as in '국지적으로 비가 오다', for things that happen only in some areas. '국부적' suits a single part, while '국지적' suits regions. The opposite is '전국적' (nationwide).

examples.en: In winter I bought and ate chrysanthemum pastries on the street.
These chrysanthemum pastries have red bean paste in them.

examples.ko: 국화빵이 따뜻할 때 먹으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The chrysanthemum pastry tastes better when it's warm.
Please give me one chrysanthemum pastry too.
Chrysanthemum pastries differ from fish-shaped pastries only in shape.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 국화빵 가게는 항상 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: The chrysanthemum pastry shop in front of the school always has a long line.

explain: 국화 모양 틀에 반죽을 붓고 속에 팥 같은 것을 넣어 구운 겨울 길거리 간식이에요. 비슷한 간식인 '붕어빵'은 물고기 모양이라서 모양으로 구분해요. 두 간식 모두 겨울에 길에서 팔아요.
explain_en: It is a winter street snack baked in a chrysanthemum-shaped mold, with filling such as red bean paste. The similar '붕어빵' is fish-shaped, so you tell them apart by shape. Both are sold on the street in winter.

examples.en: We learned in history class what militarism was.

examples.ko: 군국주의 때문에 많은 나라가 큰 아픔을 겪었어요.
examples.en: Because of militarism, many countries suffered great pain.
That film is about criticizing militarism.

examples.ko: 군국주의적인 교육을 다시 해서는 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think we must never do militaristic education again.

examples.ko: 일본 군국주의에 대한 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a book about Japanese militarism.

examples.ko: 군국주의로 흐르는 사회를 걱정하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people worry about a society drifting toward militarism.

explain: 역사 수업, 뉴스, 책에서 나오는 말이고 보통 비판하는 분위기로 써요. '일본 군국주의'처럼 앞에 나라 이름을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 토론에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It appears in history classes, news and books, usually in a critical tone. It often comes with a country name, as in '일본 군국주의'. You will meet it more in writing and debates than in daily conversation.

examples.en: He finished the work without a word of complaint.

examples.ko: 군말을 하지 말고 시키는 대로 해요.
examples.en: Don't grumble, just do as you're told.
If there's too much needless talk, the story gets long.
Complaining is no use, so stop the grumbling.

examples.ko: 월급이 적어도 군말 않고 열심히 일했어요.
examples.en: Even with a low salary, he worked hard without complaining.
That person helped without saying a word of complaint.

explain: 꼭 필요하지 않은 말이나 불평 섞인 말을 뜻하고, 대부분 '군말 없이'로 나와요. '군소리'와 거의 같게 쓰지만, 일을 시킬 때 '군말 없이 하다'가 특히 자주 들려요. 보통 말하는 사람이 못마땅할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to unnecessary or grumbling words, and mostly appears in '군말 없이' (without a word of complaint). It is used almost the same as '군소리', but '군말 없이 하다' is especially common when someone is told to do a task. The speaker usually sounds a bit displeased.

en: military service number; military serial number

examples.en: I received my service number when I enlisted.
He showed me the necklace with his service number on it.
My grandfather still remembers his service number.
Please write your name and service number on the form.
Once your service number is checked, you can go in.
What soldier doesn't even know his service number?

explain: 군인마다 따로 받는 번호로, 입대할 때 받아요. 학교에서 받는 '학번', 회사에서 받는 '사번'처럼 '번'이 붙는 말과 비슷해요. 군대 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the number each soldier gets when enlisting. It is similar to other words ending in '번' such as '학번' (student number) and '사번' (employee number). It comes up often when people talk about the military.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 군사적 긴장이 높아졌어요.
examples.en: Military tension rose between the two countries.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 군사적으로 매우 중요한 곳이에요.
examples.en: That island is a very important place militarily.

examples.ko: 군사적인 방법만으로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't solve the problem with military means alone.
We have to solve it in a non-military way.
The internet originally started for military purposes.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 군사적 가치가 높아서 관리가 엄격해요.
examples.en: This area has high military value, so it is strictly managed.

explain: '군사'와 관련된 일이나 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, 뉴스와 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요. '군사적 긴장', '군사적 목적'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미거나 '군사적으로'로 써요. 반대로 쓰는 말은 '평화적'이에요.
explain_en: It describes things connected to the military and is common in news and explanatory writing. It modifies a noun, as in '군사적 긴장' and '군사적 목적', or becomes '군사적으로'. A natural opposite is '평화적' (peaceful).

en: short of money; lame (of an excuse)

examples.ko: 요즘 살림이 군색해서 외식을 못 해요.
examples.en: Money is tight these days, so I can't eat out.
That excuse is too lame.
Even though he was short of money, he always smiled.
His excuse sounded weak.

examples.ko: 군색한 처지가 되어 친구에게 돈을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I ended up in a tight spot and borrowed money from a friend.

examples.ko: 이유를 대면 댈수록 말이 더 군색해졌어요.
examples.en: The more reasons he gave, the weaker his words became.

explain: 돈이나 형편이 넉넉하지 않아 불편할 때도 쓰고, 변명이나 이유가 억지스럽고 부족해 보일 때도 써요. '가난하다'보다 조금 점잖게 돌려 말하는 느낌이 있어요. '궁색하다'라고도 써요.
explain_en: It can describe being short of money and having a hard time, or an excuse that looks forced and weak. It sounds a little more indirect than '가난하다' (poor). It can also be written '궁색하다'.

examples.en: Stop the grumbling and do as you're told.
Don't go on with your useless talk.
There was so much needless talk that the meeting got long.
Stop the chatter and let's start with the work.

examples.ko: 불만이 있어도 군소리 한마디 안 했어요.
examples.en: Even though he was unhappy, he didn't say a single complaint.
The child took the medicine without any fuss.

explain: 쓸데없는 말이나 불평을 가리키고, '군소리하지 마', '군소리 없이'처럼 자주 써요. '군말'과 거의 비슷한데, 말투가 더 가볍고 구어에서 자주 들려요. 부탁이나 지시를 하면서 조금 짜증 난 느낌으로 쓸 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to needless talk or complaints and is often used as '군소리하지 마' or '군소리 없이'. It is nearly the same as '군말' but sounds lighter and shows up more in spoken language. It is often used with a slightly annoyed tone when giving a request or order.

examples.ko: 우리 집에 군식구가 한 명 늘었어요.
examples.en: One more extra person has joined our household.
I stayed at my friend's house as an extra mouth to feed.
Don't think of yourself as a burden, and make yourself comfortable.

examples.ko: 식구가 늘면 군식구 취급 받는 것 같아 미안해요.
examples.en: I feel sorry, as if I'm being treated like an extra person when the household grows.

examples.ko: 형 집에 군식구처럼 얹혀 지내서 눈치가 보여요.
examples.en: I'm living at my brother's place like a hanger-on, so I feel awkward.
That person isn't an extra, they're our family.

explain: 한 집에 함께 살면서 밥값이나 집값을 크게 내지 않는 사람을 조금 낮게 말하는 표현이에요. 그래서 '군식구'라고 부르면 서운하게 들릴 수 있어서, 자기 자신을 겸손하게 말할 때 더 자주 써요. '식구'는 같이 사는 가족이고, '군'이 붙으면 덤으로 붙은 사람 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a slightly belittling word for someone who lives in a household without paying much for food or housing. Calling another person that can sound hurtful, so it is more often used humbly about oneself. '식구' is a family member living together, and the '군' prefix gives the feel of someone added on as an extra.
